answer: Alliance Family Health Center is a Federally Qualified Health Center Look-Alike, serving a medically underserved community without the benefit of annual Section 330 Health Center Program (New Access Point) grant funding. Unlike many federally funded health centers, AFHC must sustain its mission primarily through patient service revenue, strategic partnerships, grants, and responsible stewardship of programs such as 340B.  The 340B Program is not simply a pharmacy program, it is an essential component of our ability to fulfill our mission. Savings generated through the program are reinvested directly into the operation of the health center, allowing AFHC to expand access to comprehensive primary care, women's health, behavioral health, pharmacy services, care coordination, and other enabling services for patients regardless of their ability to pay. Since becoming a Look-Alike, AFHC has navigated extraordinary challenges, including the COVID-19 pandemic, while continuing to grow access to care, expand services, and strengthen the healthcare safety net within our community. Despite not receiving an opportunity to apply for a New Access Point award since 2019, the organization has remained financially responsible, expanded patient access, and continued investing in quality improvement, workforce development, compliance, and innovative programs designed to meet community needs. Every dollar generated through the 340B Program is reinvested into our mission. These resources help offset the cost of caring for uninsured and underinsured patients, support the infrastructure required to operate a comprehensive community health center, and enable AFHC to continue delivering high-quality, accessible healthcare to the patients and families who rely on us every day.

Alliance Family Health Center does not segregate 340B savings into a separate fund. Consistent with HRSA guidance, 340B program savings are incorporated into the organization's operating revenue and are used to support the health center's mission of providing comprehensive healthcare services to medically underserved populations. Savings help offset the costs of uncompensated care, expanded access to services, workforce, quality improvement activities, and other operating expenses necessary to maintain and enhance patient care.
